feedback: Iteration 0 is the only raced design. It scored 26.04 and went off track in all 60 trials on oval, s-bend and slalom, with progress 0.035 to 0.115 and one line-loss event per run. Max error sat at about 0.061 m, just past the 0.06 m limit, and rms error was about 0.03 m. Steering oscillation was low (about 0.07), so the failure looks like a slow steady drift off the line, not jitter. The candidate changes only the controller, so the race isolates the controller. Its contents are valid: base_speed 1.3, kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.15, line_loss last_direction, and geometry unchanged. The ki of 0.3 is inside its 0 to 5 range, and the integral clamp of plus or minus 2 bounds its contribution. Nothing is obviously broken, and it addresses the drift that iteration 0 showed. The main risk is that base_speed 1.3 is below the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s, so completion is unlikely even if the robot stays on the line. This is early exploration with ten iterations left, so racing it is more informative than another round of reading. Do not expect the rationale's predicted outcomes to hold until the race reports them. After the race, decide from the measurements. If progress reaches about 0.995 with no line loss, raise base_speed toward 1.8, since speed is then the binding limit. If the robot still drifts with a steady bias (max_error near 0.06 with line_loss_events of 1 or more), raise ki before touching kp, since the 2% motor mismatch is the suspected cause. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 after kp went up, raise kd before lowering kp.
requested_changes: If the race shows progress at or near 0.995 with no line loss, raise controller.base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.8. Iteration 0 showed off-track exits at progress 0.035 to 0.115, so speed is only worth raising once the robot stays on the line.

If the race still shows a steady drift (max_error near 0.06 m with line_loss_events of 1 or more), raise controller.ki from 0.3 toward 0.8 to 1.0 before changing kp. Iteration 0 had ki 0 and drifted off in every trial, which points to the fixed motor mismatch.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 after kp went from 2.5 to 3.0, raise controller.kd from 0.15 toward 0.25 before lowering kp. Iteration 0 had oscillation near 0.07 and kd 0.05, so the stiffer kp is the likely source of any new jitter.
